answer: Because the entropy is measured at the cipher gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the oasis audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 4 bits per word is rejected before grading, because it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. A farm emitting 39 variations of one paragraph hence pays for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the bridge panel. That is 10 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
